summary: John R. B. Campbell works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisors Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, having also studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and others.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, McRae earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Cornell (~1988–1995), Indiana University (~1995–2005), and Komazawa University, and served as professor at Soka University (attested 2008).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Newman completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He was an assistant professor of Asian religions at the New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Carter studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard (doctoral work ~1968–1972 under Wilfred Cantwell Smith). He was a professor at Chapel House at Colgate University (~1972–2006).

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Strong studied at Hartford International University (~1970–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1977 under Frank E. Reynolds). He was a professor at Bates College (~1978–2017) and a Fulbright fellow in Ceylon (1987).
Active in Indology and history/archaeology, Shore succeeded William Jones and served as president of the Asiatic Society.

A scholar of Indology and religious studies, Hawley studied at Amherst College and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1969–1977). He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1975–1978) and as professor at Columbia University (from ~1986).

Working in Indology and philosophy, Taber completed his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He held posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1991) and the University of New Mexico (~1991).

Platts was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Balliol College (~1881–1884) and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford (~1880–1904).
Specializing in Tibetology and history/archaeology, Bellezza studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He held an affiliation at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Pettit completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and pursued doctoral studies under Robert A. F. Thurman. He also studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1985–1990) and Ashok Gangadean.

Schroeder is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oregon under Don Levi (~1990–1996). He taught at Oregon, College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).
Spellman was an Indologist and historian who held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and the University of Windsor, where he was a professor (~1967–1999).
Wilson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1819–1828). He served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842).

Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888). He served as a judge at the Calcutta High Court (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Oxford (~1923–1930).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Hiraoka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1943–1948) and Kyoto University. He was a professor at Otemae University (attested ~1966 and 1987) and held a post at Shuchiin University.

Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT (~1964–1971), and learned under Philip Kapleau, Jack Kornfield, and Joseph Goldstein. He founded and served as Professor of Medicine Emeritus at UMass Chan Medical School (attested 2016).

Ganeri, a specialist in philosophy and Indology, studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash (~2013–2015), NYU (~2013–2020), and the University of Toronto (~2020).

Silk earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at Western Michigan (~1995–1998), Yale (~1998–2002), UCLA (~2002–2007), and Leiden University (~2007).
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Gold held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).
